✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Simple task to exercise condition checking and a bit of basic geometry.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: I this contribution is intuitive and fun with a little big of challenge inside easy for beginners to understand and great for advanced Codinians for a little challenge.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: This contribution is approuvable because the tests are good formulating and the goal is very clear.

In addition to the comments as suggested by @5DN1L, please state how the diagonal lengths of each face are to be computed in the Goal section. Although this might seem trivial, we should never expect the player to have the required mathematical knowledge for the clash.

Please also add an additional test case that involves intermediate values exceeding the maximum value of an integer and causing integer overflow in typed languages.

Thank you!

Goal/Input/Constraints
* Please fix the typo: lenght => length.

Input
* This section doesn't match the actual input format. It describes a single input line, but the input actually consists of three lines. Please update this section accordingly.

Output
* This section lists "Regular Brick" as one of the possible outputs, while the cases use "Regular brick" instead. Please make the capitalisation consistent.

Constraints
* Please change 100000 to 10000.

Stub generator
* Please use the same variable names as those used in the other sections.

Cases
* The name for Validator 1 is missing.

Thanks.

Done, thanks for the feedback! I limited int overflow for normal sized ints and not long ones since that would increase the complexity of the problem more than I think is fair for specific languages, I think you should still be able to solve it in a similar way by allocating more memory.

Thank you for the fix. May I suggest shortening the sentence explaining the Pythagoras' theorem to:

"The diagonal length [[c]] of a face with side lengths [[a]] and [[b]] can be computed via the Pythagoras' theorem: [[a]]² + [[b]]² = [[c]]²."

Note that the variables a, b, c should be formatted as [[variables]] accordingly.

Below is the updated list of issues:

Input
* Please write one description for every line, in this format:

<<Line 1>>: An integer for the [[length]] of a brick.
<<Line 2>>: (etc.)

Constraints
* Please correct the typo: lenght => length.

Stub generator
* The variables are in different order from the Input section. Which one is correct? Please be consistent.

By the way, please either remove the other contribution or change its status to Private/WIP if you still want to work on it.

Thanks.
Everything should be fixed, i also increased the limit back to 100000 to include some int overflow test cases
Int overflow 1 and 2, where you can get an overflow in auxiliary calculations
Please add a pair of Regular brick cases of mixed dimensions (e.g. length is 4-digit, width is 3-digit, height is 5-digit) to balance things out. Thanks.
Ok that should be everything then, thanks
It's fine now, but it's usually a good idea to use a random number generator instead to create cases.
